doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His trumpet books and his teaching philosophy
summary: Let's Talk Trumpet, the jazz language book, circular breathing, and that every teacher has a different way.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I want to now take all of this and tie it into jazz education. What got you started in becoming a clin[ician]? Let me ask you this – another question first. Do you think – I know of at least two books that you’ve done on trumpet. Are there more?
No. Let’s Talk Trumpet from Legit to Jazz and The Interpretation of the Jazz Language and the . . .
Do you feel that – would it be fair to say that these works are an attempt to codify jazz trumpet technique?

Not necessarily. I think we – everybody has a different system – method of modus operandi, and everybody has a different message that they want to give to the kids, but they all have a different way of doing it. All I can say is that when a teacher tells a student that this is what you have to do, that’s wrong. You don’t have to do that. You say, this is my way of doing it. I find I get better results this way. But it’s a known fact that one man’s poison is another man’s meat, and you can’t – you just can’t force a kid to do something that you think he should do, when he might find better ways and means of getting results that you want him to get.
